title: From Israel’s law to the worship Jesus brought
source_text: Ἀλλ᾿ ἐπεὶ οὐδὲν βέβαιον ἐν ἀνθρωπίνῃ φύσει, ἐχρῆν κἀκείνην τὴν πολιτείαν κατὰ βραχὺ καταφθειρομένην ἐκδιαιτηθῆναι. ἡ πρόνοια δὲ τὸ σεμνὸν τοῦ λόγου αὐτῶν ἁρμοζόντως τοῖς πανταχοῦ κατὰ τὰ δεόμενα μεταποιήσεως μεταποιήσασα, ἀντ᾿ ἐκείνων τοῖς ἀπὸ τῶν πανταχοῦ ἀνθρώπων πιστεύουσι παραδέδωκε τὴν σεμνὴν κατὰ τὸν Ἰησοῦν θεοσέβειαν· ὅστις οὐ μόνον συνέσει ἀλλὰ καὶ θείᾳ μοίρᾳ κοσμηθεὶς καὶ καταβαλὼν τὸν περὶ τῶν ἐπὶ γῆς δαιμόνων λόγον, λιβανωτῷ καὶ αἵματι καὶ ταῖς ἀπὸ τῆς κνίσσης ἀναθυμιάσεσι χαιρόντων καὶ τοὺς ἀνθρώπους κατασπώντων δίκην τῶν μυθευομένων Τιτάνων ἢ Γιγάντων ἀπὸ τῆς περὶ θεοῦ ἐννοίας, αὐτὸς οὐ φροντίσας τῆς ἐπιβουλῆς αὐτῶν, ἐπιβουλευόντων μάλιστα τοῖς βελτίοσιν, ἔθετο νόμους, καθ᾿ οὓς οἱ βιοῦντες μακάριοι ἔσονται, μηδαμῶς τοὺς δαίμονας διὰ τῶν θυσιῶν κολακεύοντες καὶ πάντῃ καταφρονοῦντες αὐτῶν διὰ τὸν βοηθοῦντα τοῦ θεοῦ λόγον τοῖς ἄνω καὶ πρὸς θεὸν βλέπουσι. καὶ ἐπεὶ ὁ θεὸς ἐβούλετο κρατῆσαι ἐν τοῖς ἀνθρώποις τὸν τοῦ Ἰησοῦ λόγον, οὐδὲν δεδύνηνται δαίμονες. καίτοι γε πάντα κάλων κινήσαντες, ἵνα μὴ Χριστιανοὶ μηκέτ᾿ ὦσι· τούς τε γὰρ βασιλεύοντας καὶ τὴν σύγκλητον βουλὴν καὶ τοὺς ἄρχοντας πανταχοῦ ἀλλὰ καὶ τοὺς δήμους αὐτοὺς. οὐκ αἰσθανομένους τῆς ἀλόγου καὶ πονηρᾶς τῶν δαιμόνων ἐνεργείας, ἐξετάραξαν κατὰ τοῦ λόγου καὶ τῶν πιστευόντων εἰς αὐτόν· ἀλλ᾿ ὁ πάντων δυνατώτερος τοῦ θεοῦ λόγος, καὶ κωλυόμενος ὡσπερεὶ τροφὴν πρὸς τὸ αὔξειν τὸ κωλύεσθαι λαμβάνων, προβαίνων πλείονας ἐνέμετο ψυχάς· θεὸς γὰρ τοῦτ᾿ ἐβούλετο. ταῦτα δ᾿ ἡμῖν εἰ καὶ ἐν παρεκβάσει λέλεκται. ἀλλὰ ἀναγκαίως οἶμαι. ἐβουλόμεθα γὰρ ἀπαντῆσαι πρὸς τὸ περὶ Ἰουδαίων ὑπὸ τοῦ Κέλσου λεγόμενον, ὅτι δὴ ἀπ᾿ Αἰγύπτου δραπέται γεγόνασι, καὶ ὅτι μηδὲν πώποτ᾿ ἀξιόλογον οἱ ἄνθρωποι οἱ θεοφιλεῖς ἔπραξαν. ἀλλὰ καὶ πρὸς τὸ οὔτ᾿ ἐν λόγῳ οὔτ᾿ ἐν ἀριθμῷ γεγόνασί φαμεν ὅτι ὡς „γένος ἐκλεκτὸν“ καὶ „βασίλειον ἱεράτευμα“ ἀναχωροῦντες καὶ ἐκκλίνοντες τὴν πρὸς τοὺς πολλοὺς ἐπιμιξίαν, ἵνα μὴ διαφθαρεῖεν τὰ ἤθη, ἐφρουροῦντο ὑπὸ τῆς θείας δυνάμεως· οὔτ᾿ ἐπιθυμοῦντες, ὡς οἱ πολλοὶ τῶν ἀνθρώπων, προσλαβεῖν ἑαυτοῖς ἄλλας βασιλείας οὔτε καταλειπόμενοι, ὡς διὰ τὴν ὀλιγότητα εὐεπιβουλεύτους αὐτοὺς γενέσθαι καὶ ὅσον ἐπὶ τῇ ὀλιγότητι ἄρδην ἀπολέσθαι. καὶ τοῦτ᾿ ἐγίνετο, ὅσον ἔτι ἦσαν ἄξιοι τῆς ἀπὸ θεοῦ φρουρᾶς· ὅτε δ᾿ ἐχρῆν αὐτοὺς ὡς ὅλον ἔθνος ἁμαρτάνον διὰ πόνων ἐπιστρέφεσθαι πρὸς τὸν θεὸν αὐτῶν, ὁτὲ μὲν ἐπὶ πλεῖον ὁτὲ δ᾿ ἐπ᾿ ἔλαττον ἐγκατελείποντο, ἕως ἐπὶ Ῥωμαίων τὴν μεγίστην ποιήσαντες ἁμαρτίαν ἐν τῷ ἀποκτεῖναι τὸν Ἰησοῦν τέλεον ἐγκατελείφθησαν.
pass_a_gloss: But since nothing is firm (βέβαιος) in human nature, it was necessary (χρή, impf.) that that commonwealth (πολιτεία) too, being gradually (κατὰ βραχύ) corrupted (καταφθείρω), be changed from its way of life (ἐκδιαιτάω, aor. pass.). And providence (πρόνοια), having remodelled (μεταποιέω) the solemn [part] (τὸ σεμνόν) of their teaching (λόγος) fittingly (ἁρμοζόντως) for those everywhere, according to what needed remodelling (μεταποίησις), instead of those has handed over (παραδίδωμι, pf.) to the believers (πιστεύοντες) from men everywhere the solemn piety (θεοσέβεια) according to Jesus; who, adorned (κοσμέω) not only with understanding (σύνεσις) but also with divine portion (θεία μοῖρα), and having overthrown (καταβάλλω) the doctrine (λόγος) about the demons (δαίμονες) on earth — rejoicing in frankincense (λιβανωτός) and blood and the exhalations (ἀναθυμιάσεις) from the savour of burnt fat (κνίσσα), and dragging down (κατασπάω) men, like (δίκην) the mythical Titans or Giants, from the thought (ἔννοια) of God — himself not caring for (φροντίζω) their plot (ἐπιβουλή), though they plot most against the better, laid down (τίθημι) laws according to which those living will be blessed (μακάριοι), in no way flattering (κολακεύω) the demons through sacrifices and wholly despising (καταφρονέω) them on account of the Word (λόγος) of God helping (βοηθέω) those looking upward and toward God. And since God wished (βούλομαι) the word of Jesus to prevail (κρατέω) among men, demons have been able to do nothing, although having moved every rope (πάντα κάλων κινέω, proverb) so that Christians might no longer exist; for they stirred up (ἐκταράσσω) both those reigning (βασιλεύοντες) and the senate (σύγκλητος βουλή) and the rulers (ἄρχοντες) everywhere and even the peoples (δῆμοι) themselves, not perceiving (αἰσθάνομαι) the irrational (ἄλογος) and evil (πονηρός) activity (ἐνέργεια) of the demons, against the word and those believing in it; but the Word of God, more powerful than all, even when hindered (κωλύω), taking the being hindered as it were (ὡσπερεί) food (τροφή) for growing (αὐξάνω), advancing (προβαίνω) spread over (νέμομαι) more souls; for God wished this. These things, even if said by us in digression (παρέκβασις), [were said] necessarily (ἀναγκαίως), I think. For we wished to meet (ἀπαντάω) what is said by Celsus about Jews, that indeed (δή, ironic) they became runaways from Egypt, and that the God-loved (θεοφιλεῖς) men never did anything noteworthy. And also to 'neither in account nor in number have they been' we say that as 'a chosen race (γένος ἐκλεκτόν)' and 'a royal priesthood (βασίλειον ἱεράτευμα)', withdrawing (ἀναχωρέω) and avoiding (ἐκκλίνω) mixing (ἐπιμιξία) with the many, so that their morals (ἤθη) might not be corrupted, they were guarded (φρουρέω) by the divine power; neither desiring, like most men, to take in addition (προσλαμβάνω) other kingdoms (βασιλεῖαι) for themselves, nor being abandoned (καταλείπω) so as through fewness (ὀλιγότης) to become easy to plot against (εὐεπιβούλευτος) and, as far as fewness went, to perish utterly (ἄρδην ἀπόλλυμι). And this happened as long as (ὅσον) they were still worthy (ἄξιοι) of the guard (φρουρά) from God; but when it was necessary that they, as a whole nation sinning (ἁμαρτάνω), be turned (ἐπιστρέφω) through toils (πόνοι) to their God, sometimes more, sometimes less, they were forsaken (ἐγκαταλείπω), until under the Romans, having committed the greatest sin (ἁμαρτία) in killing (ἀποκτείνω) Jesus, they were completely (τέλεον) forsaken.
pass_b_english: But since nothing in human nature is secure, that commonwealth too had to decay little by little and fall away from its way of life. And providence, having remodelled what was solemn in the teaching of the Jews where it needed remodelling, so as to fit people everywhere, has handed on, in their place, to believers drawn from people everywhere the solemn worship of God in the way of Jesus. He, adorned not only with understanding but also with a divine endowment, overthrew the teaching about the demons on earth, who delight in incense and blood and the fumes that rise from the reek of sacrifice, and who, like the Titans or Giants of the myths, drag men down from the thought of God. Paying no heed himself to their plotting, though they plot most of all against the better sort, he laid down laws such that those who live by them will be blessed, never flattering the demons with sacrifices and wholly despising them because of the Word of God, who helps those who look upward and toward God.

And because God willed that the word of Jesus should prevail among men, the demons have been able to do nothing, though they have tried every means to see that there should be Christians no longer. For they stirred up those who reign, the senate, the governors everywhere, and even the peoples themselves, all of them unaware of the irrational and wicked working of the demons, against the word and those who believe in it. But the Word of God, mightier than all, even when hindered, taking the hindrance as food, so to speak, for its growth, went forward and spread over more and more souls; for God willed this.

Even if we have said this by way of digression, we have said it, I think, of necessity. For we wished to answer what Celsus says about the Jews, that, as he would have it, they were “runaways from Egypt,” and that these men, beloved of God, “never did anything worth mentioning.” And to the claim that they “were of no account or number,” we say that, as “a chosen race” and “a royal priesthood” (1 Peter 2:9; Exodus 19:6), withdrawing and avoiding mingling with the many so that their morals might not be corrupted, they were guarded by the divine power. They neither desired, as most men do, to win other kingdoms for themselves, nor were they forsaken, so as to become easy targets for plots because of their few numbers and, as far as their few numbers went, to perish utterly. And this held as long as they were still worthy of God’s protection. But when, as a whole nation that was sinning, they had to turn back to their God through hardships, they were forsaken, sometimes more and sometimes less, until, under the Romans, having committed the greatest sin in killing Jesus, they were forsaken completely.

choices.choice: 'the solemn teaching of the Jews' to 'what was solemn in the teaching of the Jews' (τὸ σεμνὸν τοῦ λόγου αὐτῶν is a part of the teaching, not the whole)
'a divine portion' (calque) to 'a divine endowment' for θείᾳ μοίρᾳ; translator note updated

'laws by which those who live will be blessed, in no way flattering' to 'laws such that those who live by them will be blessed, never flattering': the participles κολακεύοντες / καταφρονοῦντες belong to οἱ βιοῦντες, not to Jesus, and καθ᾿ οὓς means living by the laws
'the peoples themselves, who did not perceive' to 'all of them unaware': οὐκ αἰσθανομένους covers rulers, senate, governors and peoples alike, not the peoples only
Put Celsus's repeated charges 'runaways from Egypt' and 'never did anything worth mentioning' in quotation marks, as in 4.31, with Origen's 'beloved of God' left outside them

Recast the clumsy result clause on few numbers: 'so as to become easy targets for plots because of their few numbers and ... to perish utterly' (εὐεπιβουλεύτους ... ἄρδην ἀπολέσθαι; they, not their numbers, are the subject)
'had to be turned back' to 'had to turn back' (middle ἐπιστρέφεσθαι)
Checked 1 Peter 2:9 (γένος ἐκλεκτόν, βασίλειον ἱεράτευμα) and Exodus 19:6 LXX (βασίλειον ἱεράτευμα); both match

'a chosen race' (γένος ἐκλεκτόν) and 'a royal priesthood' (βασίλειον ἱεράτευμα) are quoted together as in 1 Peter 2:9; the second phrase is Exodus 19:6 LXX and the first also Isaiah 43:20 LXX, so 1 Peter 2:9 is cited with Exodus 19:6. 'the solemn worship of God in the way of Jesus' renders τὴν σεμνὴν κατὰ τὸν Ἰησοῦν θεοσέβειαν (literally 'the solemn piety according to Jesus'). 'a divine endowment' renders θείᾳ μοίρᾳ (a divine allotment or dispensation). 'teaching about the demons' renders τὸν περὶ ... δαιμόνων λόγον, the received account that demons must be appeased by sacrifice. λόγος is rendered 'teaching' (of the Jews), 'word' where it means the message of Jesus ('the word of Jesus', 'against the word and those who believe in it'), and 'Word' (capitalised) where Origen speaks of the Word of God who helps believers and who, 'mightier than all', spreads through souls; the play between message and divine Word is Origen's own. 'tried every means' renders the proverb πάντα κάλων κινήσαντες ('letting out every rope'). 'those who reign' (τοὺς βασιλεύοντας) means the emperors; the literal phrase is kept. 'spread over' renders ἐνέμετο (used of fire spreading or flocks grazing). 'beloved of God' (οἱ θεοφιλεῖς) is Origen's own description inserted into Celsus's charge, not Celsus's word. 'sometimes more and sometimes less' keeps the ambiguity of ἐπὶ πλεῖον / ἐπ᾿ ἔλαττον (degree or duration). The staged text has a full stop before οὐκ αἰσθανομένους and before ἀλλὰ ἀναγκαίως; both are read as commas, since the clauses depend on what precedes. Titans and Giants: generic reference to Greek myth, no single source cited.
